_readme: Ground truth for knowledge-base retrieval, used by evals/retrieval-eval.js.
Labels are CONTENT PREDICATES, never chunk ids. Re-chunking (the planned fix)
renumbers every chunk, so id-based labels would break exactly when they are
needed most. A case is satisfied when a retrieved chunk contains every string
in must_match, compared with whitespace collapsed and case ignored.
headline  - the answer figure is in the chunk title (embedded, easy)
body      - in the chunk body, title is topically related
deep-body - in the chunk body, title names a DIFFERENT table (the failure
mode this whole exercise exists for)
Every predicate is uniqueness-checked by `node evals/retrieval-eval.js --validate`.
A case matching 0 chunks is a broken label; one matching very many is too loose.
Predicates pair the answer figure with a topic co-term. Bare figures such as '5,81' matched 1073 chunks (random recall@10 = 31%); pairing brings that under 1%.

Expanded 2026-08-20 from 15 to 50 cases. The 35 added were mined from the corpus, not invented: each pairs a figure found past offset 1500 of its chunk with a distinctive word from the same table caption, so the pair identifies one table unambiguously. 10 further candidates were generated and dropped because no single document contained both strings. They are all difficulty deep-body on purpose — the original set had only four of those, which is the class this whole effort is about and far too few to tell a win from a loss.
